Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • **Persistence:** No evidence was found of host persistence such as systemd units, cron jobs, launch agents, or shell profile modification. Kubernetes Deployment/PVC and application “startup” settings appear to be normal deployment configuration.
  • **Lateral movement:** Kubernetes worker/serviceAccount settings appear related to the product’s worker backend deployment. The provided text does not show Docker socket access, hostPath abuse, kube-system takeover, or CI token theft.
  • **Obfuscation/loader:** The provided text does not show staged loaders or droppers using eval/exec, base64/zlib/marshal, or similar obfuscation.
  • **External downloads:** The pre-scan flagged ingress-nginx manifest application in cluster/k8s/kind/up.sh and Helm installation in Dockerfile.platform-backend; in context these look like normal development/container build setup steps and are not tied to credential theft, stealth, or automatic package-install execution.

  • The selected files appear to be Kubernetes templates, development scripts, documentation, and application configuration, and do not themselves indicate supply-chain distribution integrity compromise.
